subject.title: [Feature]: cron jobs.d/ directory support (one file per job, for NixOS/GitOps declarative setups)

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class per-job JSON directory/import surface for cron GitOps workflows, or should declaration-key CLI/Gateway upserts remain the supported declarative path?
rationale: The request is valuable but changes persistent storage/config behavior and sits against the current SQLite-canonical storage direction, so automation cannot safely choose the product contract.

options.title: Design SQLite-backed jobs.d import
options.body: Add a narrow directory/import or sync contract that feeds SQLite through declaration keys while preserving runtime state and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Document declaration-key GitOps
options.body: Treat `openclaw cron add --declaration-key` or Gateway `cron.add` as the supported NixOS/GitOps path and close the per-file runtime store direction after maintainer confirmation.

options.title: Defer storage surface changes
options.body: Keep this open as product backlog until cron storage and doctor migration policy have a clearer declarative-file roadmap.

recommendation.title: Design SQLite-backed jobs.d import
recommendation.body: Add a narrow directory/import or sync contract that feeds SQLite through declaration keys while preserving runtime state and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the current SQLite cron storage direction and the most recent declaration-key cron convergence work.
